essays.title: NETWAR! with jane and jeredino
essays.html:
synopsis: i befriend the most beautiful woman in the world and go to her psyop conference in austin, texas; there my friend jeredino and i mog dozens of retarded chuds; one of them is a paranoid schizophrenic who tries to bait me into fighting her so she can stab me; my mom threatens suicide; i learn a lot about trauma; i meet the king of the austin tech right—he’s a complete fuck-up; i get trapped in austin; i reflect on the nature of love and status.

I - jane

my friend jane is one of the most beautiful women in the world. she’s proportioned like athena giustiniani. looking at her makes it obvious why the greek and roman master-sculptors chose to mix features from both sexes. her androgynous beauty is timeless. it’s just bad luck that she isn’t currently a supermodel. unlike most transwomen, she likes being tall. in fact, she invariably wears a pair of rip-off doc martens which put her well over 6’3”. “i like it up here,” she tells me breezily. all of this—along with her flowing copper hair, her aggressive style, her ability to actually use make-up correctly, her laughter, her silliness, her flirtatious friendliness—means that everybody wants a piece of her.

jane is a “based tranny.” she loves chopping it up; she loves to banter. whenever she’s on the way to hang out with me, she sends me a photo of her listening to n3on’s single “she wanna hang with an indian.” she loves every form of brain poison. she’s a culture warrior who fights for every side. normally this would be deeply tedious in a person, but in her case it’s all fun, since she has no agenda, no hobbyhorse, and no ideology. though she was (until recently) a longtime member of the american communist party, she adores right-wingers—particularly the cancellable ones. “i’m dogwhistling in all directions!” she says with pride. she loves extremists of all types—but she loves normies too. in fact, the thing about jane is that (in an unstudied and unconditional way, usually found only in particularly meek religionists) she loves basically everyone. “jane, is there anyone you actually hate?” i asked her. she thought about this in silence for fifteen seconds, and then said, “can’t think of anyone, sorry.”

i met jane earlier this year at a month-long residency for ai doomer content creators. there we were asked to crank out short-form videos every day, ideally (though explicitly non-obligatorily) about ai as an existential risk. since the program was run by bay area rationalists (i.e., the sworn enemies of “the dark arts” of social manipulation), we were asked to think of ourselves as “providers of information,” not “persuaders” (i.e., propagandists). i, for one, think this is an important distinction, and endorse its kantian flavor: do not treat people as mere means; do not treat their minds as mere substrate for the propagation of your thoughts. i like to see myself as a truth-loving person who doesn’t treat others as substrate. but this milquetoast distinction does nothing for jane, who is unabashedly and wholeheartedly a propagandist. she loves psyops, information warfare, asymmetric memetics, netwar, infohazards, disinformation campaigns, and dark egregores. i’ve been trying to get her to read more diversely, but she insists on sticking to her diet of john arquilla essays, rand white papers, and declassified cia documents. jane’s fixation on propaganda is basically benign (because, again, she propagandizes in every conceivable direction), but it does sometimes put her in the soup. during doomer camp, she got in a bit of trouble on social media for marching at a “stop ai” protest while waving a sign which read “TOTAL CLANKER GENOCIDE”. tcg is a phrase popularized by jreg (a political “video essayist”/edgelord/larper), and is a crude riff on the neo-nazi slogan “total n****r death.” when news of jane’s sign hit X, a ton of heated discourse ensued: a bunch of geniuses (from sf tech twitter) saw her sign as definitive proof that all doomers are genocidal, edgy fanatics; a different group of geniuses (from berkeley tech twitter) excoriated jane for being a critical comms risk to the doomer cause. jane replied to them all with a hilarious video called “i refuse to be cancelled,” where she stated—correctly—that cancellation isn’t real and you can always just choose to keep on saying stuff. for my part, i don’t like this “tcg” slogan because—despite being an ai doomer—i am actually worried about model welfare (“i love my clanker stepson…”), and am repulsed by rhetoric that promotes the mistreatment of digital minds. in any case, all of this ethics-gooning is completely irrelevant to the matter at hand, because there were no nefarious intentions behind jane’s flamboyant sign. i’m not even sure there was an intention at all. when i asked her whether “tcg” means “we’re going to genocide the clankers” or “the clankers are going to genocide us,” she first did her signature bit of hitting the thinking emoji pose with duck lips and a cocked eyebrow, and then said, “either. both. neither? it’s up to you really. tcg girls in control.” to this i nodded and said, “okay, jane, nice one.”

jane had a great time at doomer camp. the month consisted of sixty fellows (mostly zoomers) stuffed onto a campus, making videos, getting wasted every night, fucking, and generally becoming fast friends. “i never got to have a ‘campus experience’ like this before,” jane said wistfully. she was spectacularly popular (as a friend, and more). jane was an instigator, a sexual altruist, who constantly tried to get other people laid. she drew the chaser out of many—men and women alike. “frankly, i’m trying to get a piece of that,” i said of jane to one of the british zoomer girls, who replied with a territorial “highkey get in line, bud.” this did not surprise me. cis women are the most shameless chasers. their persistent fantasies of getting dicked down by a beautiful woman cause them to brazenly fixate on the most dysphoria-inducing parts of a transwoman’s anatomy. transwomen in turn, while being attracted to femininity per se, dread taking on the masculine role, and find themselves attracted to the bodies of women but fearful of the contours of the lust attached. this tragicomic double illusion of compatibility and incompatibility is just one of the many facets of trannyhell. it’s quite sad to see one’s friends imprisoned there. of course, men—and particularly conservative men, as jane informs me—also crave the androgyne. everybody wants a piece of jane.

toward the end of doomer camp, jane gave a big presentation to pitch the cohort on coming to her “september event.” to an audience of about twenty fellows, jane annunciated her vision: “the ‘september event’ is a psyop hackathon, a propaganda party, a cybernetic cult incubator, and you are ALL invited. i’m going to put four hundred people in a massive warehouse in austin, texas, and we’re going to spend a weekend forming cults and building PLURs—plural virtual intelligences, that is—collective agents—intelligent systems of networked actors. historically, humans and livestock together formed many plurs—transanimalistic beings of conjoined agency; nowadays, humans are cybernetic: we form decentralized plurs with technology and with each other. humans spread information via genes and memes; plurs spread information via memes, but also via ‘temes’—technological, synthetic memes. crystallized ‘hard’ memetics, objective facts about the social graph that implement the agency of a meme. so, at the september event, you’ll be put into groups, and then you’ll form plurs, and then you’ll figure out what psyop you want to unleash on the world. first you’ll wage memetic warfare, and then—once your plur has spread its tendrils into the world—you’ll wage temetic warfare. this is part of a larger movement (a new religion!) to evolve from homo sapiens to homo cyborg. it all goes back to the research john arquilla and david ronfeldt did at the rand corporation on network-warfare, a.k.a. NETWAR! we live in a networked world, and if you want to influence it you have to become a netwarrior, but no one can become a netwarrior alone—you must form a cybercratic swarm if you want to engage in noopolitik. plurs and cults are ultimately the same thing, so don’t fear the plur. just get plurtarded with it. t-girls in control. the ‘t’ in ‘tranny’ stands for temetics. okay, here’s vanguard.”

at this point in the presentation jane gave way to her boss—the man financing the whole september event, a nondescript fella, distinguished only by his signature yellow hat, the man known as “discourse vanguard,” or simply vanguard. he was thin and unassuming, clearly modest by nature. he had the habit of pausing for minutes at a time in order to collect his thoughts in silence.

thus spoke vanguard:

“the world exists in a state of information fragmentation. we’re accelerating into ever greater information decentralization. but not many people are clear-eyed enough to realize that this means we need to promote our network-level cognito-tools to tier-one, fundamental concepts in our epistemic ontology.

[…pause…]

i’m interested in how memes become agents, and how these agents fight, merge, bargain, mutate, ally, blackmail, destabilize, parasitize, and breed with each other.

[…pause…]

we need to understand how bad psyops work so we can fill the internet with good psyops. to replace the infohazards with infoblessings.

[…pause…]

here’s what the memetic landscape looks like.”

vanguard pulled up a vast vertex-edge graph, with its various subregions circled and labeled things like doomerism, accelerationism, tech-rightism, and so on. i couldn’t figure out what the vertices and edges actually corresponded to (tweets and retweets, maybe?).

“now, that’s the static picture. here’s what the landscape looks like over time.”

vanguard played a video of the graph in motion, seething with life. its various subregions moved around like independent organisms, and they consumed each other, and collided, and metastasized, and bred. it pretty much looked like gameplay from agar.io.

after the presentation, a gaggle of fellows huddled around jane and made excited promises to attend her wacky event. some probed to see if she would toss in free plane tickets as a sweetener.

she waved me over.

“so, are you coming?” jane asked.

“wouldn’t miss it for the world,” i said in a mood of perfect innocence.

II - jeredino

by september, all the fellows have flaked out on jane except for me and jeredino lavagnino (“jeredino the jenius,” i call him). jeredino is a young blogcel who has spent the last two and a half years in a logorrheic frenzy, compacting his voluminous zoomeroid memories into a series of scintillating blog-gems. he’s a great lover of the picaresque novel, and is always contriving to decant himself into picaresque situations. he’s a rogue—the rare sort of rogue who is equal parts gentle and irresponsible. he wants to be always laughing, reading, drinking, gaming, or adventuring—and little else. he has minimal interest in women (“i’m uninterested in foidslop…”). a friend of mine, who feels ambivalent toward jeredino, once pointedly informed me that “he has a slight homeless energy.” this is apt, because (despite his consistent cleanliness) jeredino’s alcoholic-bum aura is greatly amplified by the beguiling cephalic fact that when he laughs (which he does frequently and explosively) the curve in his lips makes it look like he’s missing his two front teeth. jeredino strives for quality in his writing: he refuses to write “substack slop,” or “gender slop,” or “cate hall inspo slop.” in my opinion, he’s the greatest living travel writer under ninety (unfortunately, calvin trillin is still alive). unlike me, jeredino refuses to indulge in style over substance. “if the content is shit, the writing is shit,” he says. first he adventures, then he can write. recently, he’s been feeling like he’s squeezed himself completely dry, and needs to top himself off with more shenanigooning before he can resume his blog-gooning. consequently, he’s been on the lookout for a fresh “content farming” opportunity, which he’s now sure jane’s september event will prove to be.

“this is going to be a fucking disaster,” jeredino tells me, “i guess we could just leave the event halfway and go on a barbecue tour instead…”

over text, jeredino and i trade info about the event. the luma page has fifty people registered—far short of the touted four hundred. most ominously, the page says there won’t be any food or drink, but “tables and chairs will be provided.”

the psyop con (which they’re now calling “the last psyop”) is just a weekend, but i plan on spending a full week in austin because i’m certain jeredino and i will come up with some retarded side quests (e.g., spy on joe rogan’s compound? crash an alpha school? introduce jeredino to bjj at b-team?). jeredino managed to secure some free lodging for the two of us with his childhood friend noah, a certified chiller. noah and his fiancée jacqueline live out in garfield, texas, which is only a 19-minute drive from downtown austin, but somehow 110 minutes away by public transit (this devilish fact will later prove decisive—file it away in your mind). our hosts are a pretty picture of suburban domesticity: they work together as IT professionals for the austin independent school district; they maintain a small social circle, mainly consisting of jacqueline’s family; noah is an urbanism nerd who misses walkable cities but has reconciled himself to the charms of suburban texas (“at least they build housing here, and the gas is cheap,” he tells me ruefully in his car as we turn onto a massive highway interchange); jacqueline likes creamsicle moonshine, embroidery, and hate-watching “pop the balloon or find love” while ripping that friday-night zaza; they have three aquariums and are looking to add a fourth; jacqueline runs hot and noah runs cold—and they are perfect together. it was clearly his and not her idea to have jeredino around. the three of them ran in the same undergrad social circle; reminiscing about that time causes a great thaw in noah’s spirit—a revival of feeling, more than nostalgia. jeredino is still young in a way noah no longer is. by contrast, jacqueline disapproves of jeredino, which she makes known (within the bounds of hospitality). before jeredino arrives in austin, noah and jacqueline take me out to lunch at kerbey lane (a 24-hour restaurant with a vast and bizarre menu, an austin classic, which now has that polished and alienating private-equity feel). there she gripes to me about jeredino. “last time jeredino was here,” she informs me while stirring a chip into a bowl of vegan cashew queso, “he said he got ‘a sweet deal’ on a one-way ticket and hadn’t booked a flight back to oregon. well, that didn’t work for me. it’s like, ‘what? do you live here now?’ so i sat him down and didn’t leave until he bought a damn return ticket. mind if i stir this in?” jacqueline points a chip at the guacamole region of the queso. “yeah, go for it. typical jeredino,” i say while prodding at my wonton, tangerine, miso-sauce asian kale salad covered in shaved parmesan and slices of rare steak. “i’m sure he didn’t mean anything by it. jeredino is just a bit impulsive,” says noah, over a plate of eggs benedict.

the weekend is filled with many four-way car convos, typically involving jacqueline silently roiling in the passenger seat while noah and i indulge jeredino’s monologuing. “eggs benedict?” jeredino roars during one ride, “i’m a fiend for eggs benny. there was a year where i would cook not two, not three, but four eggs bennies for myself every morning. i got fat as fuckkk. it’s a very technique-driven dish; not many people are prepared to do what it takes to get a true emulsion going. the trick is to use a whole fucking stick of butter. there are too many cowards in this sauceless, butterless world…” jacqueline stares at the clouds and says, “oh lord, what is he talking about now…” i start daydreaming about jane, and how she likes making herself a bagel at 2 am (“…but i got a bagel going!” she protests before i drag her to my room). we drive up into an overpass dwelling in a forest of overpasses, and jeredino interrupts himself: “ah…! what a beautiful interchange. you can really feel the texan spirit from up here. let’s all enjoy this in silence.” noah pipes up, “yeah, these crazy texas interchanges would put even robert moses to shame.” the mention of moses makes jeredino think of robert caro, which in turn makes him think about the patron saint of our trip: lyndon b. johnson.

jeredino rhapsodizes. “lyndon b. johnson. oh yes. we can’t miss out on lyndon b. johnson. i would like to return to the lbj library. perhaps there we could enjoy ourselves in lady bird johnson’s office, or admire the acoustics of the lady bird johnson auditorium, or visit the oval office replica that for some reason is 7/8th scale… of course, the real johnson-heads—the true johnson-pilgrims!—all head west to hike the trails of johnson state park, or, even better, to walk the dusty streets of johnson city, texas… that’s the birthplace of lbj, by the way. and no, johnson city is not named after lbj. it was named after his uncle, james polk johnson. lbj was born into the poor, loser branch of the family. imagine the humiliation. growing up being one of the poor johnsons in johnson city, texas.”

this catches my interest. “i didn’t know lbj was born poor like that. well, we gotta go to johnson city then,” i say, “imagine the remnant aura. the whole city must still be suffused with lbj’s will to power.”

jeredino nods. “you’re right. we must go to johnson city.” he starts shouting, “johnson city!”

johnson city is on our lips all weekend. it’s our arcadia, our rosebud. we—exiles in this postlapsarian world—can’t help but yearn for “afters in johnson city.” i pull up instagram to watch all the johnson city reels i can find. “look at all this beautiful nature,” a foidic texan influencer says as she’s standing in an overgrown lot. there’s even a castle in johnson city—parapets and everything—which houses (castles?) a wine emporium. “of course johnson city would have a castle,” says jeredino, smouldering with desire, “we must see it. noah! on monday you will take us to johnson city.” jacqueline’s hatred waxes.

III - psyop, E-volved

the surface temperature of venus is 740 K, easily hot enough to melt lead and zinc. while nothing similar to terrestrial life could survive on the surface of venus, it is conceivable that exotic thermoacidophiles thrive in its upper atmosphere. now, if you can imagine that, you can imagine life in austin, texas. my ethnically ambiguous ass is cooking on this pavement. austin’s heat lacks the joyous aridity of inland los angeles. texan air is muggy—it feels full and in-your-face like you’re being smothered by a 20% opacity airbag. sadly, my self-narrative is that i’m a guy who likes every city he goes to, so i psyop myself into believing i actually enjoy the absence of unencumbered breathing.

day 1 - wampooming

it’s friday at 5 pm. noah and jacqueline drop jeredino and me off at a nondescript warehouse in the middle of downtown austin. we’re here to do a check-in, followed by a brief “team identity formation” exercise. there are only two cars parked out front. “judging from the car situation, no one’s fucking here…” says jeredino, “let’s say hi to jane, schmooze for fifteen minutes, and then go get some barbecue.” i say the bbq tour will have to wait because we gotta support our girl no matter what. the door to the warehouse antechamber is open, blasting unlimited cool air to the street. there’s a security guard sitting at a desk, languorously scrolling on his phone. i temporarily forget how language works, so i point at myself and say, “i go in?” he nods and waves us through. we walk into the main warehouse, which is indeed large enough to fit four hundred psyopers. there are six tables set up in the middle of the space (tables and chairs were, in fact, provided), where sixteen people are yapping away. pushed against a far wall is a table holding markers, flashcards, and a lonely box of supermarket cookies.

“oh, bu-RUH-tha, it’s so fucking over,” jeredino exclaims (this “buRUHtha” thing is a new bit he’s trying out for the weekend). i wave at jane, who is holding some sort of epic, tridentate streaming gimbal. she’ll be livestreaming the whole weekend to a small but loyal chat, an elite few. though jane publishes a fuck-ton of short-form video, she’s really more of a livestreamer by temperament. when hanging out irl, she even calls her friends “chat” to keep her streamer muscles twitching.

“what the fuck is up, jane the brain,” i say, “what’s the play, what’s the play?”

“holy shit, chat, i can’t believe you’re here,” jane squeals.

realizing that she’s talking to us, jeredino and i give jane a hug, which is returned one-armed due to the aforementioned gimbal.

“how’s the vibe in here? i’m trying to get retarded with you this weekend,” i say.

“yoo chiiiiill,” jane says, laughing.

“yeah, we’re going to go to johnson city later. wanna come?” jeredino asks.

“johnson city?” she asks.

as jeredino explains the johnson city lore, an attractive middle-aged woman comes up to me and asks, “hey, do you want some water?” i’m quite excited about this because i was led to believe only tables and chairs would be provided, so i hop on this unhoped-for potatory opportunity straightaway. i follow her to a back room which contains only a refrigerator, an ice merchandiser large enough to step inside, and a single rotisserie chicken sitting half-eaten on a countertop. i grab a water bottle out of the fridge and say “wowie, thank you” to the lady. she nods benevolently.

jeredino and jane come into the room. “hey, jeredino, there are some white claws in the fridge,” i say.

“excellent…” he says, “jane, i’m going to drink five of your white claws now.”

“sure, but there are not that many, so don’t let everyone else know,” jane says, before leaving with the middle-aged woman. jeredino sips on his pineapple-flavored claw and stares at the suspiciously jeredino-sized ice merchandiser. “yeah, i’m going to get in this thing. hold the door open for me.” i open it and see about six bags of ice inside. jeredino eases one leg in. while he’s still finding his balance on the crunching ice, the middle-aged woman returns, this time accompanied by a tall fella.

“oh, sorry. i was curious about what’s going on in this icebox,” jeredino says, stepping back out. “austin’s so fucking hot, you know…” he adds. neither of the two strangers seems put off by this at all, so jeredino casually exits the room with his claws. the tall fella inspects me for a beat and then says, “you should have some of my chicken—walmart chicken, with flour tortillas. delicious.”

“nice. thanks,” i say, “i’ve stopped eating chicken for effective-altruist reasons, but thank you, thank you. that does sound good.”

the man nods. “i’m avi. the production wizard of the event. if you need anything filmed—aaaaaaanything—i got you covered,” he says in an oscillating accent i find hard to place. is he affecting a mid-atlantic accent? or have i just forgotten how new englanders speak?

“okay, avi, sure. i’m vishal, jane’s friend. i’m going to go drink with jeredino now, see ya.”

jeredino and i sit far apart from the other psyopers. jane passes out some flashcards and tells us to write our name and our “cognitive culture.” i scribble “vishal, rationalist”. jeredino gets up, sits adjacent to me, and jots down “jeredino, rationalist-adjacent” (“get it?” he giggles). avi passes out some papers describing a sort of psyop scavenger hunt (aping uchicago’s scav hunt) with zany objectives like “get a photo of your team name at the north pole.” i give it a once-over and then toss it, while jeredino subjects his to intense scrutiny.

jane demands the attention of the room and says, “avi just passed out some papers. you can just ignore those. right now, we’re going to split into two groups, and you’ll spend the next hour building your team identity, a.k.a. your plur…! then, once you’ve settled on an identity, you’ll start working your psyop.” i’m put into a group with jeredino, vanguard, the middle-aged lady from earlier, a chud in a suit, another chud in jeans, and a black girl wearing a serafuku. jane pulls me over and says, “please be nice…” i assure her i will with a winsome wink.

i miss the first thirty minutes of the team identity formation exercise entirely because i take a meeting which i frankly didn’t try very hard to shift around. by the time i return, there’s a chudly theological debate unfolding. the middle-aged woman is popping off hard: “recall that the opening of the declaration of independence discusses the ‘laws of nature and of nature’s god.’ what exactly are the ‘laws of nature’? i’ll tell ya, it’s not what they teach you in church—and definitely not what they teach you in school. in fact, the powers that be are trying their hardest to suppress knowledge about the laws of nature. i made many freedom of information act requests to force the government to release any and all documents pertaining to the ‘laws of nature and nature’s god,’ but i’ve been refused every time. i’ve called many, many governmental offices, but they all reject me. the sad truth is that they can’t be honest, even if they wanted to. natural law is the true, highest law of the land, and the language in the opening of the declaration of independence is an explicit reference to the two row wampum treaty, which is the highest law because it was not only a promise made to the iroquois confederacy, but to ‘all indians,’ and indeed to ‘we the people’… every american should read the two row wampum treaty—it’s the only way to heal this nation. our current system denies the living law, the law of nature, the nature movement, its herbalists and midwives and healers and everything else.”

one of the chuds speaks up, “i get all that, but you’re forgetting one thing: christ jesus is lord. america is not going to be healed through indian medicine magic. we will be redeemed only through iesus nazarenus rex iudaeorum.”

but the lady came prepared: “ah, but a careful, scholarly reading of the bible shows that these two laws are not different. if you read genesis carefully, after cain kills abel, god tells cain ‘the voice of your brother’s blood is crying to me from mother earth.’ mother earth. the earth is feminine in the bible! that’s nature’s god.”

the chud nods. “i’ll have to check that verse more carefully…”

jeredino is patiently soaking it all in, but i can’t take any more. demoralized, i open my laptop and start reading emails. twenty minutes later—after drifting in and out of group consciousness—i listen to them debate the merits of the crusades. i don’t see myself forming a plur with any of these goofs. i get up and walk to the far wall to inspect the lone box of supermarket cookies. my retatrutide is hitting hard, but through sheer willpower i force myself to eat a depression-cookie.

jeredino and jane join me, and we huddle up.

“the chuds are firmly in control, jane,” i say.

“and that black girl in the school uniform was just doomscrolling the whole time…” jeredino adds.

“oh yeah that’s maye. she’s a black white supremacist,” says jane.

“sorry, what?” i ask.

“a black white supremacist,” says jane.

“how does that work?” i ask.

“maye hits the hard-r really hard. she has 100k followers on X. it’s sort of a larp, maybe?” jane says.

i pull up maye’s twitter. the content is mainly her bed-ranting into the phone. the first video i see is titled “we really need to start lynching these N****Rs!!” most of the comments are from guys with roman statue avis, saying things like, “you are my nubian queen... miscegenate with me NOW!”

i look over at our team, and the middle-aged lady is talking about the laws of nature and of nature’s god. “wow… that old woman is really wampooming,” jeredino says.

jane looks a bit nervous. “yeah so… what do you think about her?” she asks.

“she seems nice,” i say, “i’m just not in the mood to debate theology in that low-competence way right now.”

“she’s great,” says jeredino, “she’s really carrying the team. the chuds aren’t coming up with anything at all… at least she has some ideas. i’m thinking our psyop should be like something out of the da vinci code. you know… we’re on the hunt for the declaration of independence, but it turns out the real declaration of independence is the two row wampum treaty… maybe the real declaration of independence was the two row wampum treaty we made along the way…”

i notice a box on the table filled with about a hundred green hats. they’re gatsby green… they fill me with hope.

“jane, are these for us? i want one,” i say.

“go for it. i printed those last year and they’ve just been sitting in my closet ever since. i brought them to austin all the way from fucking virginia,” she says, laughing.

i pull one out of the plastic wrap and squint at it. the hat reads “MAKE E GREAT AGAIN” (the Es are printed so close together that it looks more like “MAKEE GREAT AGAIN”).

“what the fuck is this? MEGA?” i ask.

“MEGA,” jane affirms. i give jeredino an e hat.

“look at us, two e-boys,” i say, “but seriously jane, what is this? explain please?”

jane pulls up a three-thousand-word wiki page she wrote on nexus.libertymyself.com. it begins:

What does it mean to Make E Great Again?

The genius of MEGA lies in its deliberate openness. E has many interpretations: Economic Liberty, Earth Relationship, Entropy Management, European Autonomy, Estrogen Wisdom…

the scales fell from my eyes. something about this fEEls right to me… the three of us start riffing about “E”: e is environment, e is estrogen, e is eusocial, e is empathy, e is eugenics, e is everyone and everybody and everything, e is earth, e is estonia, e is victor-e, e is tran-e, e is e-commerce, e is 'egelian dialectics, e is…

i begin to hear the wind whispering a promise of something e-xtraordinary.

day 2 - the whiteness of the wall

jeredino, our hosts, and i have a leisurely barbecue lunch, and after we finish around 1 pm we return to psyop con. to my and jeredino’s horror, everyone else is still sitting around and fucking debating. there are two big groups now, both “working” on their “psyops.” the first is dominated by a guy ranting about how progressives need to be psyoped into believing in “scientific” racism (a.k.a. human biodiversity). this group is workshopping a meme they’re calling “hbd jesus,” which i guess is just jesus but he’s based and racist now. personally, i don’t get it. one of the great appeals of christianity is that it gives you terra firma to dismiss out of hand the materialist case for racism. the biblical guidance is clear: “there is neither jew nor greek, there is neither slave nor free, there is neither male nor female; for you are all one in christ jesus” (galatians 3:28). what’s the point of giving this up? anyways… after a little bit, the alpha-chud moves on to argue that africa needs to be recolonized “on humanitarian grounds” due to the difference in iq between races. i conclude that either this guy wants to turn the event into a weekend-long based ritual, or he just loves low-iq iq debates—so i just permanently tune him out of my mind. the other group is led, unsurprisingly, by the two-row-wampum lady (who, it turns out, is actually jane’s mom), and she’s basically just reiterating her standard homily. yesterday i found this dull but charming; today i find it completely repugnant. it’s a horrible thing to watch someone hammer away this much on a single topic. i like the conspiracy fox (e.g., jane), but not the conspiracy hedgehog (e.g., jane’s mom).

it seems jeredino and i will simply have to make our own fun. while most of the room is content to sit in a circle and jaw on lobotomistically about race realism, we will be going all-in on “E.” going absolutely e-tarded.

the first order of business is we must explain to jane’s mom that we won’t be wampooming with her anymore. “i just don’t really see the concept here,” i tell her, “the ‘natural law’ stuff isn’t much of a psyop, is it?”

“no, there’s a lot to it,” jane’s mom insists.

“sure, i believe you. let’s see… could you give me something to work with? got any memes? give me a meme or two,” i demand.

jane’s mom thinks for a moment. “there’s a saying i came up with: world peace starts in the bedroom,” she says, stony-faced.

“nice,” i say, “yeah, that’s funny. it’s kind of raunchy, sure.”

“got it. i think we’re going to work on ‘E’,” i say.

with a childlike look of consummate sadness, jane’s mom says, “so you’re not doing natural law anymore?” o misery, misery…

with that, jeredino and i kick off our e-nanigans. i find a movable wall in the warehouse. with green crayola markers, we draw a ten-foot-tall E on a piece of paper, tape it to our purloined wall, and wheel the whole ensemble right behind the race-cels—E looming over them. mogged. next, we get our friend tomás to create an astonishing playlist of suno-generated e-nthems, which we start blasting from a pair of bluetooth speakers. we contemplate requisitioning the warehouse on the last day to throw the world’s very first “e rave.”

in “whitehaven,” jeredino and i film a masterpiece. jane works the camera for us and captures a ton of dynamic, e-nergetic shots. later that night i edit it, and…

our undeniable charisma begins winning people over. leo, an immense and powerful vibecoder, is the first to don a MEGA hat. e-tard after my own heart, he immediately goes to pump.fun to mint a shitcoin simply called “E”.

based leo is heading to the airport. he doffs his MEGA hat and goes, “take it E-asy gentlemen…” i suppress a tear. with leo gone, the only people i’m interested in are jeredino and jane. i’m just waiting for the event to wrap up so the three of us can engage in some e-pic tomfoolery.

we make a plan to head to johnson city early the next day. i try to yap more with jane, but she gets commandeered by a highly clouted “hegelian e-girl,” who sits her down for a friendly lecture on the nature of e-girl statusmaxxing:

all this excitement around mr. gray has my interest piqued… he’s an amateur geneticist, a pillar of texas tech-right community, someone i’ve followed for a long time via his blog, his podcast, and his twitter. i’ve learned quite a lot from him. he’s a bit of a degenerate. bumping rails at his house is an austin rite of passage. there’s loose talk about a party happening tonight at mr. gray’s. this i have to see. what i didn’t realize then, in my innocence (“as naïve as only a pervert can be,” as humbert humbert said), was that i was about to have the worst night of my life…

interlude - a call from mom

but before getting into all that, i want to describe an episode from the middle of psyop weekend which caused me immense mental damage, and inflected the proceedings with enduring melancholy.

it’s the lunchtime of day two—before we returned to the warehouse—and noah, jacqueline, jeredino, and i are lunching at rollin smoke bbq, a counter-service joint in downtown austin. “the first leg of our epic barbecue tour,” says jeredino. just as we’re about to order, i get a surprise call from my mom. she’s been recovering from a recent heart surgery, which was quite safe (“only a 1% chance of death!” the surgeons assured), but the whole saga was quite grave, for had her doctors not caught the problem with her valves when they did, my mom would have been dead within the year, guaranteed. this whiff of death offends me: though my mom has just turned seventy, in my mind she’s always fifty.

i can tell from the jump that something was wrong.

“do you need any money?” she asks.

“uh, no. i could be more liquid—but no. why?” i ask.

“i’m thinking about wrapping things up here,” she says.

“like, selling all the chicago apartments?” i ask. her side project for the last decade has been the buying, renovating, and renting of condominiums.

“no. wrapping up everything,” she says.

i’m walking around the parking lot, idly weaving between cars. i stare at the cracks in the pavement.

“so… what are we talking about here? suicide?” i ask.

“i can’t take it anymore,” she says.

now this is new. my whole family has off-distribution borderline personality disorder, meaning that the four of us take turns feeling acutely betrayed and then epicly crashing out on each other. i used to think this was fun and quirky, but now i see it as just another pathetic fact about the limits of our nature. bpd is 40-50% heritable, and most of the rest of the variance is attributable to non-shared environment, so there just isn’t much space for poor parenting decisions to explain what went wrong with my sister and me. in any case, i find myself on the receiving end of a maternal crash-out about once a year (pretty low, all things considered). the playbook is simply to nod along and wait things out, but now my normal confidence is shaken because my mom has never once threatened to kill herself before.

“i can barely get up without my heart rate spiking,” she continues, “this is not living, it’s not… i’m trapped here.”

“you told me your recovery was going well. what happened?” i ask.

“i don’t tell you everything. it’s… time for me to go,” she says.

“hm. well, okay. i can’t tell you what to do. i’m going to buy a ticket to chicago to see you,” i say.

“no. do not come. that would ruin your weekend.”

“i think i should be allowed to talk with you before you kill yourself,” i say.

“no. you are not allowed to come. i’m telling you not to come.”

“well, i don’t think that’s a fair thing to say,” i say.

i’ve somewhat quickly made peace with the notion that it’s not my place to command my mom to not kill herself—but maybe i could get her to change her mind by hanging around and jestermaxxing for her for a couple months. i miss chicago, and think it’d be nice to cook for her again. despite being a millionaire off of amd stock, my mom lives (as junior soprano would say) like a poveretta. living in a tiny apartment with her again—surrounded by our extremely racist black neighbors who regularly tell my mom to “go back to china”—sounds pleasant to me right now, as i think i’m overdue for a break from californian bliss. shouldn’t let yourself be happy for too long. i get an acute flash of anger at my sister, who hasn’t talked to my mom in four years, due (unsurprisingly) to retarded bpd reasons of her own. because of this, my mom has never met her three grandchildren. surely some sociopathic therapist (or priest, possibly) has talked my sister into this being a good idea, a healing idea. despite some turbulence, my mom has been a good mother, far better than most, far better than almost all asian mothers, one who didn’t tiger mom us, who told us to live passionately, who encouraged me to be an actor and a philosopher when i wanted those things (and who correctly told me to be a quant or a machine learning engineer when i no longer did), who taught me how to earn more than i spend, and who only hit me twice. why is my sister so resentful? well, i suppose oldest children tend to get the worst of it (whatever “it” is). but the real reason is that it’s just so easy to convince yourself that cutting your parents off, tokyo-story style, is an integral part of your healing journey. o misery, misery…

“and your daddy yells at me,” she screams. this comes as a great relief. evidently, she’s bpd-spiking at my dad, and is just giving herself relief through suicide-talk. my dad texts me, “momma needs to vent. just listen.”

“he shouldn’t do that,” i say.

“he gets mad at me for not cleaning the apartment, but i can barely goddamn move,” she says. these days, gaps in her english appear only when she tries to curse.

“okay, mom. okay. it’s going to be okay. i won’t come to chicago. don’t worry. but if you do decide to do something like that, you have to promise to tell me. i do have the right to talk to you before you die.”

“…okay,” she says.

“i love you, mom. i’m going to go now.”

i walk back over to jeredino, noah, and jacqueline, who have been waiting for me.

“just had a wild conversation,” i say.

“oh?” says jeredino.

“my mom’s talking about killing herself,” i say.

“oh,” says jeredino.

“it’s fine, she’s not going to do it. but she’s never threatened suicide before. i don’t know what to think about this,” i say.

jeredino walks us over to the counter.

“yeah… you can’t let them use the suicide card. once they start on that, they never stop. i’m thinking we split this pit smoke meat master special, it’s only thirty-seven bucks, and has a bit of everything,” jeredino says. he has a schizophrenic brother, so he knows what it’s like being put through the wringer.

the outdoor space at rollin smoke bbq is quite nice: a tented area with a bunch of lawn chairs, gigantic fans spraying mist in all directions, and a forty-foot screen playing an espn documentary on longhorn football. it’s peak america, and i’m sinking into my lawn chair, mopily pondering what the world would look like with my mom dead. i’m basically still a child: to me, my mom is always young. it was essentially luck that we caught her heart issues in this otherwise-fatal year (the mechanism had been misdiagnosed several times over the last decade—even during the surgery itself, her doctors encountered a couple surprises). more than merely prosecuting a crash-out, she was trying to acclimate me to her being gone.

with mist cooling my head, i recall a decade-old dream: i’m in minnesota, in the driveway of my childhood home, in early spring, with its willows and its rhubarb, and there’s my mom standing behind me, telling me to pick up a log.

“i can’t do it, it’s too large,” i tell her.

“just try,” she says.

i bend over and fail to lift the log.

“no i really can’t do it.”

“just try.”

i bend over and fail again.

“you’re not listening. it’s not a matter of trying—it cannot be done by me.”

“that’s okay, just try.”

i bend over, and this time i’m screaming in the struggle.

“goddammit. fuck you. you’re not listening to me. you never listen. i told you i—”

i turn around to face her, but she isn’t there. i remember then that she’s already dead.

i can’t picture a future where my parents are dead, but i can always picture this dream.

“mmmmm, nice brisket,” says jeredino.

“i’ll trade you all these wings for some brisket. i stopped eating chicken. for effective-altruist reasons,” i mumble.

IV - knife play

evil queers? queerness appeals to a certain type of predator. this is a bayesian point: it’s not that being queer means you are likely to be a psychopath, but conditional on being a psychopath, you are much more likely to shroud yourself in queerness. queers are depressive, frequently suicidal, separated from their parents, in need of stewardship, tolerant of pariahs, sexually available, endlessly yearning... this is superior terrain for an apex predator. jane says the signs of queer evil are written on the face. she warns me when she catches a glimpse of it. “that’s an evil tranny for real,” jane says, “you can tell by her physiognomy.” with all due respect, i object to this methodology. maybe the signs are indeed obvious, but they are not etched into bone and cartilage. they’re located in the liminal behavior—the slip of the mask, when the psychopath’s eyes retreat into stony coldness, and her brows knit as if to say “you’re just a heap of meat to me. an obstacle.”

mary is this type of psychopath. she is gaunt and smug, and her main social posture is to neg people in nonsensical ways. her cheeks are sallow, and her wrists are scarified. she likes to show strangers her knives. she’s a paranoid schizophrenic. she says she’s on the run from the government. she says the feds have depersoned her by confiscating her passport (in reality, she mailed her passport to some government agency that won’t reissue it without her birth sex printed on it—a “depersoning” of a sort for sure, but this is not what mary means).

no one knows much about mary. she found out about the last psyop by lurking jane’s livestreams. she seemed normal, more or less, during the event—just a bit rude and unfunny, with the occasional flash of malice. jeredino and i didn’t interact with mary much because she was a partisan of team hbd jesus. our infrequent attempts to put her on that e-shit were met with quips like, “e is weak,” “e is my enemy,” and “who are you…?” one time she stuck her nose close to jeredino’s shirt, snarled, and said “this embroidery is so fucking ugly. what are you doing?” after she left, jeredino grumbled, “look who’s talking... she’s dressed like shit...” on the first night of the con, while out with the psyoppies at a japanese restaurant, out of nowhere, mary took off my MEGA hat, stared icily at my face, and asked, “who are you? who are you...?” i ignored her, since i thought she was attempting some sort of lame status-aikido. only later would i realize how lucky i was to leave uncut: there is currently a document in circulation compiling evidence that during her time in austin, mary kidnapped some poor transgirl and tortured her all weekend.

4:30 pm - “not my fucking scene”

let’s move back to the present tense. it’s 5 pm on sunday, and the last psyop is finally over. i’m hoping that all the fuckhead npcs will voluntarily dissipate, leaving jeredino, jane, and me to go get white-girl wasted, maybe score some 2cb, shoot the shit, and scheme about tomorrow’s long-awaited expedition to johnson city. “ahh! i can practically taste it,” jeredino says as he scrubs around johnson city on google maps.

alas! we leave the venue with a party of seven: me, jeredino, jane, jane’s mom, avi, psycho mary, and a dutchman in a cowboy hat who goes by the name of preet. due to his long hair, preet was the mascot for team hbd jesus. unlike his teammates, he felt the e-nergy, and would observe jeredino and me with puppy-like curiosity. despite this definitive proof of good character, preet does not spark joy, since he (i’m sorry to say) is not a sparkling conversationalist. perhaps the only nederlander who does not speak english fluently, preet’s effect on conversation is to slow it down 40% as he tries to clarify something that doesn’t need clarification.

the magnificent seven go to grab dinner at a casual restaurant of my choosing, a nearby georgian spot specializing in khachapuri. “mmmmMMmm… sumptuous cheese-slop,” coos jeredino, inspecting the menu. the restaurant is counter-serve, and we’re taking turns languidly ordering our food. mary slinks next to me and tenderly pets me on the pate. the waitstaff put together a long table for us inside, but we take so long ordering that another party sits down and takes it from us. this fires mary up.

“they took our table…!” mary tells the waitress.

“sorry, ma’am, we’ll put together another one for you,” the waitress says.

“i need to get THE FUCK out of here. this isn’t my fucking SCENE,” she yells before running out the place.

i look at avi. “is she gone?” i ask.

“so it appears…” he replies.

the waitress puts three tables together width-wise outside. as soon as my butt touches metal, avi goes from 0 to kindergarten teacher again for some reason: “get up. this table should be rearranged,” he says.

“why?” i ask, sipping water.

“because it will improve the flow of the restaurant,” he says.

“can we just sit and relax? it’s been a long day and i don’t think it matters,” i say.

“it matters because i asked you to do it,” avi says.

“okay, avi, nice one. sure,” i say as i unc-edly rise back to my feet. avi rotates the table to be long instead of tall, and i sit down again with his permission.

the khachapuri is quite nice. i wanted the base model: just bread, egg, and cheese—all goop. but jeredino objected and said we should share one with “more protein in it” (why though? we’re both fat fucks…), so we ordered a variant where half the cheese is replaced with ground meat. luckily, this didn’t end up undercutting the goop-factor that much, so i’m a happy camper. avi gets some georgian white wine for the table. the bottle boasts that georgia has the oldest unbroken winemaking tradition (“8,000 years of craft, perfected!”). i take a sip and am repulsed by its oppressive insipidity—it’s the flat soda of whites. even the white zone had more body and character.

when the waitress brings preet his meal he stops her with one hand without looking at her, and stares with great intensity at his tea. moving slowly, he grips his tea hard in one hand, and transmogrifies his stop-sign hand into a forklift structure fit to receive the oblonginous khachapuri platter. the logistical kabuki he’s performing, and the gravity with which he lurches through it, suggest to me that this is a man who has too few hands. accordingly, i grab his teacup and move it out of the way.

“do NOT... touch...” preet snaps.

“ah!” i say.

i release the cup, embarrassed. i’m contrite for my clumsy imposition. i realize now that preet has intense ocd, and that his dishware tai chi is part of a compulsive ritual. i slump into dejection. i’ve just been subjected to three separate sperg-outs in under twenty minutes. i’m deeply regretting this trip. it feels like my social status is tanking in real time. everyone at this event seems to suffer from at least one debilitating darkest-dungeon-style nerf to their mental stability. i get on my phone to send jeredino a message on signal.

avi has barely touched his food. he’s been on his phone, texting mary. after twenty minutes he gets up and says, “i shall meet mary at a kratom bar.”

“okay,” says jane, “text me the addy and we’ll link up later. afters at the kratom bar, wooo!”

once avi departs, jeredino, jane, and i have a luxurious, ninety-minute dinner. jane’s mom is off in the corner, wampooming at a hunk she met earlier today; preet is quietly enjoying his meal and occasionally weighing in with gems like “what? please repeat.” we three e-tards are free to talk about what we like—and what we like is writing. i’ve been trying to get jane admitted to a month-long writing retreat i’ll be running this coming november. i can’t just hornily wave her into the program, because i believe in these deeply fake things called “fairness” and “objectivity,” and accordingly i need her writing samples to actually impress my four reviewers. sadly, her first application was roundly rejected (receiving almost the lowest score among all applicants) due to her samples being sketchy, semi-schizo, and filled with typos. pretty much all her writing is about netwar, which also did not impress the reviewers. in setting up this system, i have potentially denied myself a month in paradise with the world’s most beautiful hunnie—cockblocked myself—destroyed and betrayed myself for nothing. luckily, i had one last trick, which was to tell her to take two months, study prose a bit, and then reapply to the residency.

“have you done your homework? i told you to read orwell’s ‘why i write’ and didion’s ‘why i write.’ what did you think?” i ask jane.

“i tried. i tried sooooo hard. i tried at least five times—each! but i couldn’t get more than three paragraphs in. they’re just soooooo boring. it’s like ‘what the fuck are these people talking about?!’” jane says. she sinks into her chair, pouting.

“no good!” i say with a laugh, “to write you must read.”

“my writing can’t be that bad...” jane says.

“no. it is bad, jane. the style is all over the place,” i say.

“what does that mean though?” she asks.

“it’s a bit... schizo...” jeredino says.

“but that’s just how i think,” jane says, sinking harder, pouting harder.

“that’s okay, but writing is not like thinking. your prose needs more connective tissue. like look here,” i say, pulling up her writing on my phone. “in your piece about our doomer video residency, you write...”
